title: Locate invalid bytes
lead: An invalidUtf8 issue (and a stray-byte charset kept under the stray-byte tolerance) carries firstLines and the byte offsets of the first invalid sequences, and names the layout region each falls in (preamble, annotation, header, data). The descriptor says plainly when the charset label was kept despite invalid bytes. **Not in this slice:** repairing or escaping the bytes.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Today the issue says only how many invalid bytes there are. A consumer that accepts stray bytes in a preamble but not in data cannot tell where they are without rereading the file, and its refusal message can only name the count, not the line. Found in a consumer review, 2026-10-30, on padded preamble files where one preamble key holds a corrupted byte.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - The byte pass and the sniff (`src/squalify/Sniff/ByteSniffer.cs`, `Text/InvalidUnicodeScanner.cs`: invalid-byte offsets already exist), `Profiler` (the `invalidUtf8` and `invalidUnicode` issues; region lookup after the layout is known), the issue and encoding models and `DescriptorWriter` (`issues[].regions`, optional `encoding.invalidBytesTolerated`), docs/descriptor.md (issues, encoding, key order, consumer subset, versioning-policy sentence), design.md, user-guide.md; the sq-12 schema (waits on this slice) must carry the members

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A delimited file with one invalid byte inside a preamble key: `invalidUtf8` carries `offsets`, `firstLines` and `regions` (one region name per offset, same order, from the layout region kinds: preamble, annotation, header, units, data), here `preamble`; a stray byte in the header line gives `header`, in a data record `data`; several bytes give one region each.
- A file whose charset label is kept under the stray-byte tolerance: `encoding.invalidBytesTolerated` is true; it is absent when there are no invalid bytes and when the tolerance is exceeded (the charset then becomes latin-1).
- The caps of `offsets` and `firstLines` bound `regions` too (same length as `offsets`); a byte outside every region (for example after a cut) is named as the nearest region or `other` (state the rule; the implementer decides and documents it).
- UTF-16 and UTF-32 `invalidUnicode`: the same `regions` (offsets exist); a file without invalid bytes is unchanged: goldens change only for fixtures with invalid bytes (list them).
- Determinism: the same bytes twice give the same issue.
- Mutation-check each test.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests above.
2. After the layout is known, map each reported offset to its region (preamble, annotation, header, units, data; decide the rule for offsets outside every region and for multi-block files, document it) and write `regions` next to `offsets`; write `encoding.invalidBytesTolerated` only when true.
3. Docs in the same change; review any golden diff (only fixtures with invalid bytes may change).
